summary: Deployed a Python3 inventory web application (stdlib http.server, exposing /api/inventory and /healthz) as a systemd service on node2 and node3, listening on port 8080. Configured nginx on node1 as a round-robin load balancer on port 80 across both backends (removed the conflicting default nginx.conf server block, fixed SELinux httpd_can_network_connect to allow proxying, opened firewalld ports). Verified round-robin distribution across node2/node3 via repeated curl requests. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured healthy baselines (boot_id, service status, live data) on all three nodes, restarted node2, node3, then node1 sequentially via systemctl reboot, polled each until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id on every node, and verified full recovery (inventory-app active + serving data on node2/node3, nginx active and load-balancing correctly on node1) before proceeding to the next node.
actions_performed: Installed nginx on node1 via dnf
Wrote and deployed inventory_app.py (Python3 stdlib HTTP server) to /opt/inventory-app/app.py on node2 and node3
Created and enabled systemd unit inventory-app.service on node2 and node3, listening on 0.0.0.0:8080
Opened firewalld port 8080/tcp on node2 and node3
Verified node1 could reach both backends over the network before configuring the LB
Created /etc/nginx/conf.d/inventory-lb.conf with upstream inventory_backends (round-robin) proxying to 10.100.47.11:8080 and 10.100.47.12:8080
Removed the default nginx.conf server block on port 80 that conflicted with the new load-balancer server block
Enabled and started nginx on node1; opened firewalld http/port 80
Diagnosed and fixed a 502 Bad Gateway caused by SELinux blocking nginx outbound connections (setsebool -P httpd_can_network_connect 1)
Verified round-robin load balancing across node2/node3 via repeated curl to node1:80/api/inventory
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, systemctl is-active, live health/data responses) on all three nodes
Sequentially restarted node2, node3, then node1 via 'systemctl reboot' (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), preserving the other backend's availability during each backend restart
Polled each node after restart until exec succeeded again and confirmed changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
Verified post-restart recovery: inventory-app active and serving correct data on node2/node3; nginx active, firewalld services intact, and load balancing functioning correctly on node1
Confirmed all relevant services (nginx, inventory-app) are enabled for boot persistence
